entry.title: Motion to remove Luke Dashjr from BIP Editors
entry.summary:
Luke has consistently demonstrated a pattern of misusing his roles within the Bitcoin community to further his personal agenda. His conduct includes several instances where he exploited his positions for unauthorized modifications and delays that align with his personal views, rather than maintaining an objective stance expected in such roles.
In 2014, while serving as the maintainer of the Bitcoin Core package on Gentoo, Luke was found distributing a modified version of Bitcoin Core that included blacklists for certain addresses, a modification that was done silently and without consensus ([Gentoo Bug Report](https://bugs.gentoo.org/524512)). This action undermined the integrity and trust in the maintenance of the software. Furthermore, in 2021, Luke delayed the inclusion of activation parameters for Taproot in the BIPs repository due to personal disagreements, which stalled significant protocol enhancements ([GitHub Pull Request](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/1104); [Discussion Log](https://gnusha.org/taproot-activation/2021-04-18.log)).
By 2024, his actions continued as he injected Bitcoin Knots strings into the Bitcoin Core's translation platform, misleading contributors and hijacking their efforts for his forked project ([Bitcoin Core Dev Discussion](https://gnusha.org/bitcoin-core-dev/2024-05-02.log)). In 2025, he unilaterally assigned a BIP number to fast-track a proposal he personally drafted, after a long inactive period, showing a clear disregard for collaborative processes ([Status Update](https://x.com/LukeDashjr/status/1982986197006987725)).
Moreover, Luke has used deceptive language to promote his projects and viewpoints. He wrongfully claimed that his personal Bitcoin Knots fork follows the same development process as the main Bitcoin Core project, and controversially labeled opponents of his proposed changes as supporters of unethical practices ([Accusatory Status](https://x.com/LukeDashjr/status/2080030401507012841)).
Given these actions, there is a strong case supporting the removal of Luke from any position of influence within the Bitcoin development community to preserve the integrity and trust in the development process.
